Chevron markings on a fracture surface are a definitive indicator of fatigue crack growth. Taken together, the beach marks and the chevron pattern show that the crack grew progressively under repeated pressure cycles in service; in other words, the flaw extended incrementally as a result of cyclic loading during operation. Surface morphology, however, settles only the mechanism of growth and not the origin of the crack within the joint, and it is the origin that separates a flaw present from the moment of welding from one nucleated in a sound profile by service stresses. Because metallographic sectioning through the weld reveals the weld bead geometry and heat-affected zone microstructure, the sectioned material confirms the position of the crack initiation site relative to the weld fusion line and the heat-affected zone, which investigators accordingly establish. Radiographic films taken at fabrication document the as-built condition of the weld, and that documentary evidence indicates that the non-destructive examination performed at commissioning establishes a baseline flaw size for the weld. Fracture mechanics calculations estimate the time required for a flaw of given initial size to reach critical size. After those fabrication-stage films were taken, a successful hydrostatic proof test at commissioning demonstrates that the weld contains no fabrication defects. Destructive examination of the failed seam established that the weld contained a lack-of-fusion flaw left at fabrication, and a joint certified defect-free by proof test cannot be squared with a joint carrying an unfused root at that same location, so one of the two findings must give way. The operating history records that the vessel was operated through more pressure cycles than its design fatigue life allowed; at least one of these two conditions obtained in this case, the unfused root left by the fabricator or the exhaustion of the design cycle allowance by the operator, and perhaps both did. Because the unfused root was present in the joint as welded, the review board determined that the crack initiated at an undetected fabrication flaw rather than at a service-induced initiation site; the cycle overrun, by contrast, told against the operator's stewardship of the vessel without bearing on the question of where the crack began. The metallurgical and documentary records thus converge, and responsibility follows from the location of the origin rather than from the vigour with which either party argues."
